The test image shows a corn leaf with elongated, narrow, tan/light-brown lesions oriented parallel to the leaf veins. Multiple lesions visible on a dark green leaf. Key features: elongated rectangular shape, tan-pinkish color, vein-parallel orientation.

Top candidates: Gray Leaf Spot (rectangular tan lesions parallel to veins), Northern Leaf Blight (elongated cigar-shaped lesions), Eyespot (small oval lesions), Holcus Spot.

Let me view one reference from each of 4 candidates.

Analysis:
- **Test image**: Elongated, narrow, tan/pinkish-tan lesions running parallel to leaf veins on dark green corn leaf. Multiple lesions, clearly vein-bounded rectangular shape.
- **Eyespot**: Many small circular/oval yellow spots with dark centers — does not match.
- **Holcus Spot**: Single round pinkish-white lesion — shape doesn't match (round vs elongated).
- **Northern Leaf Blight**: Shows larger, more diffuse blight areas — not matching.
- **Gray Leaf Spot**: The elongated, rectangular, vein-parallel tan lesions in the test image are the hallmark of GLS — lesions bounded by veins, running lengthwise along the leaf.

The test image matches Gray Leaf Spot most closely: narrow, rectangular, tan lesions constrained between veins, parallel to leaf axis.
